title: Assume only what every path guarantees
statement: Assume only what every path guarantees: each branch teaches what later content uses and agrees on facts, and topics another course teaches work in either order, from a new angle.
detail: A review of a reading course named its biggest problem: the child picks a character and the flow isn't fixed, so no one can be sure which knowledge or folktales a child has met, which undermines retrieval and sequencing (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/FEEDBACK-LEDGER.md`). Guidance for the reading and writing courses that carry science and social studies makes the same point across courses: with no link to the subject courses, no one can be sure whether a student has studied a topic, so topics from earlier grades are always fair game, a same-grade topic has to work whether or not its subject lesson has happened, and a lesson keeps the vocabulary, nuance and framing the subject course gave it (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/Brainlift social science and science coherence.md`). A re-encounter should feel like a new angle, not a repeat, and in science it is better to re-meet an idea from an earlier grade than to be the first place a student meets it (the same file). When an idea may come back from another course, keep that course's framing and come at it from a new angle rather than repeat it.
against: A push for much more fiction sits against the knowledge-first plan these re-encounters serve; the response to it expects the re-encounter framing to reconcile the two but logged it as an open question, "Log as a question, not a silent rebalance." (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/FEEDBACK_RESPONSE.md`). The guidance accepts a same-grade topic as long as the lesson works whether or not the subject lesson has happened yet, so a student may still meet an idea there first (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0137-science-social-studies-reencounter-guidance.qmd`).
